utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Waespi, we asked you to report on the communications between the expert, Mr. Theunens, and the Prosecution. Could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- deliver your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. I -- I did e-mail to my team and got e-mails back discussing any communications they may have had with Mr. Theunens on the contents of the report. I've received these e-mails. I have reviewed them. None of the contacts -- and there were indeed contacts on the report but none of them involved any suggestion or any due influence on Mr. Theunens, on the substance of the report. Rather, they were related to drawing Mr. Theunens's attention to typographical or translation errors. In one example, there was the numerical designation of an HV unit, the MP unit wrong, and that was brought to Mr. Theunens' attention. There was also input from the former supervisor, Mr. Phil Coo, of Mr. Theunens as to the introductory part called "Scope" in the report. You remember there were a couple of pages, I think three pages, in the final report, P1113, which addresses, you know, the scope of Mr. Theunens' report, and Mr. Coo made a few suggestions. Unfortunately, I have only seen the e-mail but not the changes to the scope but I'm confident that Mr. Theunens, who keeps his e-mails, can tell you what suggestions were made by Mr. Phil Coo as to changes in the scope in this introductory part. There were also a couple of meetings, I think two -- I know two meetings between Mr. Theunens and lawyers. One meeting was with Mr. Tieger which happened either on the 12th or 13th of December, 2007. Mr. Tieger just came back from a private emergency trip to the US, and that must have been either on the 12th or 13th December, a couple of days before we filed the actual report and that's a meeting to which Mr. Theunens referred to, and Mr. Tieger has reviewed last night's transcript and he says he has no doubt that the -- about the contents of the meeting with Mr. Theunens. He doesn't have a specific recollection of the meeting. There was a second meeting between lawyers of the trial team and Mr. Theunens. Mr. Steve Margetts and probably Prashanti Mahindaratne met with Mr. Theunens, and again, there was no undue influence, suggestions as to the contents of the report. So all these contacts the team had over time, specifically November, December of last year when the report was filed, was on accuracy. There was a long e-mail, one, two pages, by Mr. Andrei Shakhmetov, the military analyst, Mr. Theunens talked about him in his evidence, who brought quite a number of translation errors to the attention of Mr. Theunens, and I believe Mr. Theunens accepted these suggestions. This is, Mr. President, the report on e-mail contacts or other contacts between the broader team, the Gotovina team not just members of the trial team but also analysts and other members of the trial team with Mr. Theunens, on the contents, the substance of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The second meeting, Mr. Margetts, Ms. Mahindaratne, is there a date for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: We asked Mr. Margetts and Ms. Mahindaratne. They believe -- they are not sure, but they believe it might have been March 2007, so that would relate to the first draft of Mr. Theunens's report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When was the report, as it appears now, delivered to the Prosecution, including typos, whatever? So when did you receive the report which did not undergo any further changes anymore?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I have not specifically inquired, but must have been just a day or on the day it was filed, which, I believe, was the 14th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that was after the meeting Mr. Tieger had with Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: This is certainly correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, whenever you said there was no undue influence, of course, that requires a judgement, what influence is due or undue is, of course, your assessment of it. It's -- therefore, the Chamber very much -- is focussing on facts primarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. This is obviously my assessment but more importantly the assessment of the team members who met with Reynaud Theunens. I'm relying on their --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They are just as involved as you are, so that they are benefiting, as team members, from the report to the extent that the Prosecution sought this report to be produced, because the Prosecution took the position that such a report would support the Prosecution's case. To that extent, your team members and you, Mr. Waespi, are in a similar position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Maybe just one point. That two e-mails, the one from Mr. Shakhmetov and one from Mr. Phil Coo specifically state that they knew about the sensitivity of sending something to -- to the expert and they say that, of course, you know, it is up to you, Mr. Theunens, as the expert, to determine whether to accept even these typographical and other changes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before we ask the witness to enter the courtroom, is there anything in relation to what Mr. Waespi just said, that the Defence would like to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whether Mr. Waespi has any other comments to make concerning the testimony of Mr. Theunens, as to the matters that he -- he looked at, such as the indictment on one occasion, any other material details that go to the substance of this issue, in relation to Mr. Theunens's involvement with the OTP concerning this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you're referring to the genesis of the report, any context whatsoever, broad sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And may I take that you consider it to be an obligation for the Prosecution to be transparent and disclose any knowledge on that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Considering what has happened, I think it is important for Mr. Waespi to say -- state his position on it. I propose to ask further questions, having considered the transcript with my team overnight and looked at various matters, and would like Mr. Waespi to state his position as fully as possible about the involvement with -- of Mr. Theunens in relation to this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you say ask further questions, to Mr. Theunens or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I will. Whether Mr. Waespi has any other information, anything else that needs to be said, so that the OTP position is before the Court now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, is there anything that could be of relevance in this context, which we may not have asked you but what you would like to tell us, in order for the Chamber to be fully informed about every aspect of this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Not at this point in time, but given what I heard from Mr. Kay and also his reference to the indictment, I will consult with team members again, think myself whether there is anything which should be brought to Your Honours' and the Defence's attention, but there is nothing at this point I can think of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Waespi, a question. Having considered the matter overnight, and you certainly will have done it, do you agree or disagree with me if I suggest that it would have been appropriate to put specific questions to the witness at the moment where he said that there was no feedback at any later stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you for this question, Mr. President. In fact, I thought about that, I looked at the transcript, and of course it is unfortunate that this meeting with Mr. Tieger and Mr. Theunens came out for the first time in cross-examination. I was aware of that meeting, but only that it related to typographical errors and stylistic changes. That's what I heard when I prepared Mr. Theunens. When I prepared my examination-in-chief, I didn't pay any attention because for me it had no relevance as to the substance of the report, methodology, and so on. And if you review my examination-in-chief you see that I focussed, like most of us here in court, on the March 2007 report. So it didn't cross my mind. Maybe it should have. That I should also have focussed more about what transpired in December 2007, but, again, at that time, I didn't think of anything that was relevant for Your Honours and for the Defence, and if I knew at that time about the importance now placed on that meeting, I would have disclosed it in my proofing note to the Defence. That's for sure and perhaps even led it live. That's really I can say about this issue. And likewise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Listening to your answer, I do agree with you that much of the focus was on feedback on the March 2007, the unfinished report, although specifically questions were put to him in relation to later versions, and even one of the questions where -- but let's not -- I take it that we have all read overnight the transcript, also of the -- thank you for that answer. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I also read the transcript last night and one of the issues specifically for the Gotovina Defence is that in my cross-examination of Mr. Theunens, I did not pose a specific set of questions to him about his contact with members of the Office of the Prosecutor about the military police issue, which we spent a long time in cross-examination on, because I accepted his answer that he had given earlier that there was no communication; and therefore, I felt that the Chamber would not have appreciated me going back in once the witness had given an answer as broad as the answer was in the first place. However, now I believe that -- we have now passed the baton to the Cermak Defence, but I believe that the question now becomes relevant in light of the difficulty that transpired in cross-examination for the witness to accept certain propositions relating to the military police. I call the Chamber's attention specifically to the Prosecution's pre-trial brief beginning at paragraph 61 and going through paragraph 67, and the importance to the Prosecution's case of the issue of the subordination, alleged subordination, of the military police to General Gotovina. And I would like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's keep matters short. You would like to have an opportunity to put further questions on the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, what I wanted to say was, either -- if there is going to be more questioning of this witness, I don't have a problem if the Bench is going do questioning that it be put to him, Did you have any communication. And particularly now that I've heard that Ms. Mahindaratne and Mr. Margetts had a conversation with him, as far as I understand, Ms. Mahindaratne handles the military -- some of the military police issues for the Office of the Prosecutor. If the question can be put to him, Did you have any communications with anyone from the trial team about the issue of the military police; or alternatively, that I wanted to alert the Chamber, then, that I would need time for recross so that I could pose questions to the witness on this limited issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't think the Chamber will immediately put questions to the witness in relation to this. If only because I have not reread paragraph 61 to 67 of the pre-trial brief, and since you link it to that, it is it more likely that -- but we'll consider the matter that we would give you an opportunity for re-cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now very practically, when? Would that be ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't wanted to interrupt Mr. Kay -- Mr. Kay is gracious enough to -- that can I deal with it now if the Chamber wishes or whenever the Chamber pleases is fine with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I was going to deal with the drafts first off this afternoon so that we have this issue before us. If it meets favour with the Bench and it's more appropriate to compartmentalize Mr. Misetic's cross-examination to follow that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you could agree on that, what would be a suitable moment, then the Chamber will accept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May the witness be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Theunens. The Chamber asked the Prosecution to give a full report on communications team members have had with you. This has revealed that, where on earlier questions about any communication or feedback on the later versions of the report, that is, not the March version but later versions, that your answers have not given full insight in the communications there have been, especially not that you had a meeting with Mr. Tieger, as you testified yesterday, a meeting that was held before the final version of your report was delivered to the team. Yesterday quite some questions were put to you. Perhaps there may follow more questions on the matter. Yesterday I think I said that I hoped that I had missed something. You suggested that you had referred to feedback or at least communications in later stage. Everyone has reviewed the transcripts, and such a reference was not found by anyone. Therefore, where I yesterday said that I expect an expert to give us information, full information on matters which must have been clear to you that they were of interest for us to know the whole feedback issue, you, being a professional, you must have understood what it meant and have not been transparent. I earlier, once, said to you that a certain answer was evasive. You then admitted that. I would like to remind you, but with this introduction, that you are still bound to the solemn declaration that you gave; that is, that you will tell the truth, nothing but the truth, but especially the whole truth. It may be that some of the questions that were put to you earlier in the assumption that there had been no further communications between you and the team after March, that Defence counsel may want to extend their cross-examination, which looks as if it was concluded already. Mr. Kay, are you ready to continue your cross-examination? Yes, Mr. Theunens, I was informed by the Victims and Witness Section that you would like to say something about the matter. If you would please keep it brief, then you have an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I also checked the transcript, and I would like to refer to page 12160, line 8, where Mr. Kehoe indeed asks me about previous feedback or contacts with the Office of the Prosecutor. I started to answer at page 12160, line 12, and I tried to give a very detailed answer, which addressed both, or not only both but which addressed the contacts that existed at the time of the submission of the table of contents. Then I spoke about the March draft. Then I spoke about the subsequent drafts that were submitted. And then my intention was to talk about the feedback I received on the final draft. However, at page 12161, line 6, Mr. Kehoe said: "Excuse me, Mr. Theunens, I have limited time. Then I say: "Yes, but ..." And then on page 12161, line 8, Mr. Kehoe says: "So I'm going to cut you off here, sir. A second element I wish to bring to your attention is that on the request of Messrs. Waespi and Du-Toit, I prepared a -- what is called a supplemental information sheet. I have a copy of it here with me. This is the version of the 11th of November. And in that document on paragraph 23, I put the following: "Between February and December 2007, I regularly sent unfinalized drafts of the report to Alan Tieger, in order to keep him updated of my progress. I did not receive feedback from the team. I sent the final draft of the report in December 2007." And if you wish, I can explain which exact time I sent which part of the report. Anyway, going back to paragraph 23. "Alan Tieger and Prashanti Mahindaratne informed me of some typographic and other stylistic errors in this final draft." I am still convinced that this is one of the documents I signed and I'm understand the assumption that that document, I have a copy with me here, was also disclosed to the Defence. I realize that the document Mr. Misetic showed yesterday evening did not include this paragraph 23. And there are also other parts missing in relation to the methodology I applied. However, I realize that my signature appears to be on the document that Mr. Misetic showed yesterday evening in court. I realize that I should be aware of what I sign. Now, the only explanation I can find is that this document was given to me for signature by a member of the Office of the Prosecutor, and I assumed that, well, it was just another formulation of what I had put in the supplementary information sheet and therefore I signed it without controlling it. Just to close off, I wish to emphasise that I have always tried to be as a transparent as possible. I was available to meet the Gotovina Defence ten days before my testimony in the Seselj trial. I sent the drafts of my report on the same evening of the 19th of November to the court officer. I have tried to answer the questions from the Prosecution, the Trial Chamber and the Defence to the best of my abilities, and I sincerely regret that what I call or what I consider a misunderstanding has had such ramifications. There was no reason whatsoever for me to hide the contacts with Mr. Tieger or Ms. Mahindaratne in December, in particular because I had included in the information note, which under my assumption was also disclosed to the Defence. Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, are you ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The matter we're concerned with particularly is your first statement on this matter, on the 19th of November. "Now, I also want to emphasise that except for the initial tasking I received from Mr. Tieger and the sending of the draft, I had no contact with the team. I didn't receive any phone calls. I didn't receive any -- or e-mails. I heard -- when I insisted -- when I sent the draft in March 2007, I'm not sure anymore how I was informed that actually, well, forget about the deadline. You can continue. I saw my March 2007 report as an unfinalized draft whereby, okay, we had to ... fulfil certain deadlines, and I would be given the opportunity to continue work ..." That's from page 12157 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. And this answer refers to the -- to the March draft. I did not refer in that answer to the final draft in December, and if you want I can also read you out what I sent to whom at what time and during which time-period the meeting with Mr. Tieger and then it was also contact with Ms. Mahindaratne took place. I have the information with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could give us the date of the meeting that would --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is what I was going ask, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Before you give us the dates shall I, just so that we've got the fixed points in time, put the dates of your drafts to you? Would that help, Mr. Tieger [sic], because I have them here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would call Mr. Theunens Mr. Theunens instead of Mr. Tieger, that's -- especially under the present circumstances --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that would be preferred.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Theunens. Part 1, the first draft, 21st of February 2007; part 2, first draft, 12th March, 2007; second draft, part 1, 27th of April, 2007; second draft, the same date; third draft, part 1, 23rd of November, 2007; part 2, third draft, 4th of December, 2007; final report, 18th of December, 2007. Those are taken from the drafts. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. And in addition, I can mention that the meeting with Mr. Tieger must have taken place between the 6th of December and the 13th of December, 2007 -- excuse me, between 4th and December and the 13th of December, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After draft three and before final report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. The other meeting between Ms. Mahindaratne and Mr. Margetts, I believe?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember a meeting with Mr. Margetts. I remember that -- there may have been several meetings with Mr. Tieger on one day, between 6th and 13th, maybe two, or three, I don't recall exactly, and at one of these meetings Ms. Mahindaratne was present. I believe it was at the first of these -- of the two or the three meetings, which happened between the 6th and the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You refer to stylistic matters. Could you explain what stylistic matters means.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean by that what I already addressed yesterday, i.e., that this was basically the first time that somebody else than me read the report, and it was important for me to get feedback in the area of was the structure logical, the organisation of the different sections did it make sense, headings and so on in general, and there was some feedback in the area of stylistic whether, for example, if I had chosen a particular heading, to explain why I had taken or used that heading when, in the view of the reader, the part that followed was not entirely coherent or, or in line with what the heading would suggest. There were also corrections or suggestions in a sense of language, i.e., typos, some words but it was very limited. And as I mentioned yesterday, section 3 of part 2, namely the section dealing with General Cermak as the Knin garrison commander, was subject of these discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yesterday I asked you questions about the shift in the first three drafts from Mr. Cermak being civilian authority to civilian/military authority. The change in that status must then have come between the 4th of December and the 18th of December, 2007. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. It is possible that indeed during these discussions with Mr. Tieger and/or Ms. Mahindaratne the question was asked, Well, what do you mean by the title you have there. But again the titles are only an introduction or a kind of label that covers the text that follows. And I realize -- I believe, maybe I'm wrong, that the fact that I chose -- that I used the text "military authority" has created confusion. Military authority is not an official title. At least I have not found a definition in Croatian doctrine as to what military authority means. But the fact that I wrote civilian/military authority instead of only civilian authority, which did I in the earlier versions, is because from the documents I reviewed, I can see -- I saw that General Cermak was giving instructions to civilians, civilian police, civilian companies and so on, and at the same time he was also issuing military orders to the military police in Knin. There was military communication or correspondence with the Split Military District, even if it was very limited, based on the documents that I reviewed and that again, if I remember well, is the reason why I added the military after the civilian in the -- when I defined or when I had the heading civilian/military authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The footnotes and content that you had by the date of that third draft on the 4th of December were exactly the same and unchanged from the those footnotes and content that you had in the final report on the 18th of December. So in a period of two weeks, with the information exactly the same as before, and with meetings with Mr. Tieger and Ms. Mahindaratne, your report changed in a significant context, don't you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree, Your Honours. Because as I mentioned the titles or the headings, are only the -- how would I call it? Yeah, the title for what follows, the importance of the report lies in its contents. If the contents doesn't change, well, the title is just a clarification of -- of what has already been explained in the contents. It doesn't make sense, at least in my methodology, to change a title to try to, I don't know, invent something or add something if it is not supported by what is in the contents of the report. And as you mentioned yourself, the contents of that section, i.e., the footnotes and reference, have not changed. So the title for me -- I mean, the change in title, as there may have been changes in other titles, is only related to the fact that I wanted to have a title and maybe it was proposed to me to have a title that is more specific or more focussed on what follows. And I apologise for not exactly recalling which exact proposals or suggestions Mr. Tieger or Ms. Mahindaratne made in relation to titles or typos or so on. The problem I have is that I also have worked on other cases and testified in other cases, and there's only so much can I remember. And I know that is a shortcoming but it is something that I have to face and accept.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The interesting thing is that there is a heading that has been changed in the final report at page 245. You have a heading: Civilian/military authority. You've told us that the discussions with the counsel for the OTP concerned headings, matters within your report. Is this a heading that was suggested to you by them?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, it is not a specific heading or a heading that was specifically suggested to me. As I mentioned yesterday, and again today, there were -- there was discussion about or discussion -- there was an exchange of views about section 3, i.e., the Knin garrison commander section. There -- I was probably asked, Well, what do you mean by these sections or maybe you can -- is there a way to restructure it or to make it clearer to the reader, not only for section 3 but also for other sections. And again I do not specifically recall what was addressed with me for the different sections of the report. I think the key issue is, as you already highlighted, is that the contents of the section did not change.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Forgive me, the contents did change. As I put to you yesterday, Mr. Cermak moved from the first three drafts dealing with that section from civilian authority to, in the two weeks between the 4th of December and 18th of December, to civilian/military authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- that matter at least whether there is a change or not, seems to be clear to the extent that the witness tells us that this better reflects the content of the report, whether true or not is -- of course the Chamber will consider that, as you say, it is not not without significance that civilian/military is something different from civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You mentioned discussions about part 3. What were those discussions? Did they include beefing up the section concerning General Cermak to emphasise the military authority? Because, Mr. Theunens, something happened in those two weeks.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, these discussions did not include what Mr. Kay callings "beefing up" the section. What they included was to change or to see whether the structure, as it was, could be changed; for example, in order to maybe rearrange certain sections, i.e., to have a more streamlined structure. And again I don't recall --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Continue. I'm just talking to Ms. Higgins.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you did it through the microphone, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. And She's just right here as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that makes other people stop talking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For example, to try and group the duties in a manner that would make it easier for the reader to understand. But again, and I mention what you said, the footnotes, i.e., the references on which the report is based did not change. And I would consider that, at least in my methodology, is really the most important issue. Why? Because the titles are only a reflection of the contents whereby the contents is based on the footnotes. I could write that somebody was the highest religious authority, but if I have no footnotes in the report that go in that direction such a title would not make any sense, and that is the way or the manner in which I see the change of -- of that title from civilian authority into military/civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On the 2nd of December, at page 12978, you gave us a definition of what you mean by streamlining: "As I mentioned, I see these changes not as fundamental changes or changes in conclusions or changes in position. I see these changes, as I call it, a streamlining of the contents of the report." So changing the nature of the opinion you had, as to authority from civilian to military, is that something you call "streamlining"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is not what I have been saying. What I have been saying is that I have not changed my opinion or my conclusion. Actually, the conclusions I draw from the documents. The change lies in the fact that I amended the title in order to be a better -- at least in my view, a better reflection of the contents, and in relation to the discussions with Mr. Tieger and Ms. Mahindaratne, to make sure that a reader, who has not looked into the detail of the report to the extent as I did, understands the message I try to communicate through the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Now just moving to meetings. You have told us about several meetings on one day with Mr. Tieger between the 4th and the 18th of December. So how many meetings on -- on one day?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned earlier that there were two or three meetings, and I think the first one or -- if I remember well, Ms. Mahindaratne was only present at the first meeting. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Continue.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Again, if I remember well, the first meeting was a very general meeting about the report, where Ms. Mahindaratne suggested that actually the report was too detailed and covered issues that I shouldn't be covering. Like, for example, the situation between 1992 and 1994. I then said that I believed that these sections were essential and that I was in a position to address the topics that are covered in these sections. I'm not sure whether we discussed any longer but, again, I believe that I could leave the room then. I was then called back -- I don't know whether it was before noon or the afternoon or then there was only a meeting in Mr. Tieger's office with Mr. Tieger himself where he browsed or he went through certain parts of the report and to ask me, Well, what you do you mean here, or here, well, that's a typo, and it was not in a structured or organised manner because, I mean, there were still typos in it when the final version was filed. And during that meeting with Mr. Tieger himself, or only, we also looked at -- I mean, specifically for your question, section 3 and the structure of that section. There -- if I remember well, there was a third meeting that day -- or a second meeting with Mr. Tieger alone but a third meeting, overall, for the report, where maybe I showed him -- I believe I showed him the amended structure I had developed, and we had a discussion about that, or a -- and if I remember well, that was approved and then I proceeded with finalization of the report and preparation for having it ERNed and MIFed, but then that was done by a member of the team and then subsequently the report was filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And what do you mean by the structure. What do you mean by that? Let us be specific.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean by that that -- it would be easier if I had the previous draft before me, but I didn't have time to look at that. I read the transcript this morning. But if I remember well, it could be that I addressed certain duties of General Cermak at different locations within the section, whereas it appeared that after a second lecture it would seem more logical to group these duties in -- in a different manner. And I called it yesterday and today streamlining. It is maybe not the best word in English, but that is, at least from the view of the person who wrote the report, I see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm giving you an opportunity now to say what other meetings you had with members of the -- of the Prosecution, either investigators, either analysts, members of their team, whosoever in the organisation connected with this case and discussed your report with. I'm giving you an opportunity now to state each and every meeting.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to be specific, between December 2007 -- excuse me, December 2006 and December 2007?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No. I'm giving you an opportunity. Don't pin my question, please, because I would like to what your involvement has been with this case, because, as you know, we have challenged your report and we have looked at the drafts. And so, Mr. Theunens, I am asking you now and statements have been made in court to declare what that contact has been so that the Judges know.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will take the supplemental information sheet I prepared to cover the meetings between December 2006 and December 2007, and for the meetings after -- or the contacts after December 2007, I will give those from my memory. December 2006, meeting with Douglas Marks Moore, whom -- I mean, we knew each other very well from the Vukovar case, followed immediately by a meeting immediately with Alan Tieger about my experiences in UNPROFOR/UNPF. Very briefly, there was a proposal whether I could draft a report for the Gotovina et al case. Then in -- I believe it's end of December or in January I received the 10-point tasking. This was followed by a meeting probably with Mr. Tieger but also with my team leader separately, my team leader and myself separately, which was followed by a meeting --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you give the date of that meeting with Mr. Tieger and your team leader?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, the -- there was no meeting with the two of them. There was a separate meeting. There was meeting with Mr. Tieger --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you give the date?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: End of December -- no, that must have been January. In the course of January 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. And team leader.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Team leader --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I want you to be -- I'm giving you a chance, Mr. Theunens, to be as specific about every single detail on this as possible.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm seizing the opportunity now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember well, that was a week or something after the meeting with Mr. Tieger because there was -- there were discussions to which I was not privy about whether or not I should become involved in the Gotovina case at all, involvement at all or no involvement whatsoever. Shortly after -- and, again, it could have been January or February, I received a 17-point tasking. My conclusion was that the 17-point tasking, which was sent to me by Mr. Tieger, resulted from conversations Mr. Tieger had had with Mr. Coo, but I'm not sure of that. Shortly after I had a meeting with Mr. Tieger -- I'm not sure whether Mr. Moore was present, where I -- and maybe Ms. Mahindaratne was present but I'm not sure either but certainly with Mr. Tieger, where I proposed that I would compile a report having the same layout or using the same kind of methodology or template as I had done for the four other cases I had prepared reports for. That was approved. We then -- I mean, there was a deadline set of March 2007. I was also -- or Mr. Tieger told me that my only contacts with the team would go through him or through the two military analysts, Mr. Morris and Mr. Shakhmetov. I soon after spoke to Mr. Morris and Mr. Shakhmetov to talk about, Well, how are we going to organise this project. I was informed that there was spreadsheets they had prepared so the spreadsheets were sent to me. After that, I had call it irregular contacts with them, for example, when I asked them whether a translation was available or whether, as I mentioned on the first day, when I heard that they were planning missions to state archives in Croatia whether they could look for particular documents, mainly regulations. Then we have the March deadline. I sent the first draft -- or, yeah, the first draft. March 2007, I apologise. I continued to work on the report but with interruptions because I'm also tasked to compile a report for the Stanisic/Simatovic case which was filed in July 2007. Anyway, I worked also on other cases. Then, obviously, I met Mr. Tieger -- I mean not officially but when you go for a cup of coffee or you are on the second floor in the corridor you can -- yeah, you talk to each other as a matter of courtesy, but I didn't receive any instructions as to, Well, file -- your report has to be finished on date X, Y, or Z. It may be that another member of the team asked me for a draft but just for his or her personal information. Then the next meeting -- I mean, formal meeting I remember were the ones between the 4th and the 18th of December whereby I mean that they happened on one day. First one with Ms. Mahindaratne and Mr. Tieger; and the second and probably a third on that day, very briefly with Mr. Tieger. Then the report is filed. After that, there were members of the team who spoke to me but on a social basis. One of the investigators Mr. Van Rooyen, we have done several missions -- we did several missions for the Vukovar case in Belgrade, or interview missions, we went for coffee together but there was no influence whatsoever by Mr. Van Rooyen on my report as it has been filed or on my conclusions. Then in April, I'm not sure whether I was called by telephone and received information by telephone from Mr. Tieger in relation to the compilation of an addendum or whether I was called to his office, and this may have been end of March or early April 2008. But what I do remember is that on one day, I came back from a meeting for another case, and I saw -- I found a hard copy of a spreadsheet on my desk, which I believe was sent by Mr. Tieger. I don't know whether they were 50 or 60 entries but there was a heading indicating that -- or a cover page indicating that Mr. Tieger requested me to review these documents as they had been obtained as a later stage and, if necessary, include them in an addendum. In any event after the filing of the report in December 2007, I kept on looking for additional translations through the -- what is called the translation request application in the Office of the Prosecutor, and to see whether were other relevant documents which could be important for the report that had been filed. So then I -- I started with the compilation of the addendum, still working for also other cases. I'm not sure anymore when I finished the addendum but I know it took -- I was surprised it took so much time. When I -- two or three weeks before the addendum was filed. And I don't know what the reason is for that but I was a bit surprised because I found that I had worked very hard to get the addendum finished as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I could just stop you there at the filing of the addendum as our interest is earlier in the stream of events. You mentioned December 2006. What contact did you have concerning this case before December 2006?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had contacts with Mr. Shakhmetov and Mr. Morris but just in the framework of working in the same team, the Military Analysis Team, and obviously I had social contacts with other members of the Prosecution team because I know them from other cases. For example Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I understand that. Yes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really trying to think whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You see, it's the indictment that I'm coming back to, that you read the indictment once.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, the indictment I downloaded from the internet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was actually -- I mean, the recollection I have is that I did it after the first meeting or the first contact with Mr. Moore about well, whether I was -- would be interested to work on the Gotovina case --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Before the indictment was filed, did you look at it, the drafts of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No -- no, Your Honours. I want to emphasise I was not professionally involved with the Gotovina team prior to the December 2006 meeting. And on one hand, I was surprised because I thought, like, I work here for a number of years, I'm one of the few people who was in the area during the time-period of the events, and I was surprised that nobody asked me about that. But otherwise I didn't, yeah, worry about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You give a rather lengthy answer where Mr. Kay just wants to know whether you ever reviewed any --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Drafts of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- any drafts of the indictment and the answer is ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not. Your Honours, I apologise for being so detailed but I really want to avoid the experience of the 19th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the questions are clear and if the answers are just as clear, that -- it's a very factual question whether you have reviewed them yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, on those matters concerning the draft, that's all I asked and I agreed earlier with Mr. Misetic it would be appropriate for him to deal with his section of cross-examination at this stage so that it is all dealt with together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Theunens, as I indicated before, there might be some additional questions. Mr. Misetic may address concern matters he refrained from doing in his earlier cross-examination. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, first, you have now mentioned that you met with Ms. Mahindaratne in December of 2007. Mr. Waespi indicated earlier that he was told it may have been March 2007, and then at page 23, line 10, you mentioned the possibility that sometime around February of 2007 you may have had a meeting with Ms. Mahindaratne. Is it possible that in fact you've had multiple meetings with Ms. Mahindaratne about your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The December meeting with Ms. Mahindaratne is the meeting where I received feedback from her in relation to the report. I apologise, December 2007. The earlier meeting or meetings, February or March 2007, I have no specific recollection for the date, but I did not receive feedback from Ms. Mahindaratne in relation to the report during one -- during a meeting I had with her being present. She may have been present during a certain time-period during one of the meetings with Mr. Moore and/or Mr. Tieger. And Mr. Tieger, I mean. I'm not sure whether she was -- because that is something that I didn't mention because the meeting we had on the 17th of January, 17th January 2008, but I'm just trying to think whether she was present there. I'm not sure whether she was there; I don't think so. I'm sorry to be so detailed but just to answer the question. Prior to December 2007, I do not remember a meeting with Ms. Mahindaratne whereby she or during which she gave me feedback on my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Can you please identify for us everyone within the Office of the Prosecutor with whom you had a conversation about the military police generally and specifically about subordination of the military police.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prior to the filing of the report, i.e., prior to December 2007, I remember talking to Mr. Tieger, Mr. Moore, Ms. Mahindaratne, as well as asking Mr. Shakhmetov and/or Mr. Morris about the relevant regulations covering military police in general. Discussions specifically on subordination were with the three first people I mentioned. It may be that -- that a team member -- it could that be Mr. Margetts at one moment in time asked me to send him my latest draft, i.e., before the filing of the report, but he did not give me any feedback in relation to the report in general, and, of course, he didn't give me any feedback on the issue of the military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, just to avoid whatever misunderstanding, you said prior to the filing of the report, i.e., prior to December 2007, could that -- because you remember talking to Mr. Tieger, Mr. Moore, Ms. Mahindaratne. Could that have been prior to the filing of the report but still in December?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honours, it covers the time-period from December 2006 to December 2007. What I mean is that during the meetings I mentioned earlier, the topic of subordination of military police was indeed mentioned, maybe not at every meeting, but I recall certainly with Mr. Moore that we discussed that. The meeting that happened -- I mean -- or the meetings between the 4th of December and the 18th of December, 2007, i.e., the meetings whereby I received feedback on the final draft, there -- I have no recollection of any discussion on the subordination of the military police during meetings during the -- the time-period between 4th December and 18th of December, 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was discussed? You mentioned now: "The topic of subordination of military police was indeed mentioned, maybe not at every meeting, but I recall certainly with Mr. Moore that we discussed that." Tell us a little bit about that discussion. What was discussed?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned, Mr. Moore -- I assisted Mr. Moore in the Vukovar 3 case and there we had a situation which could be considered similar in a sense. We had a use of the military police by the Guards Motorised Brigade of the JNA in Vukovar and, of course, the events that occurred at Ovcara. And there was also the issue of professional and the operational line in relation to the subordination of security organs in the JNA. And I remember a conversation with Mr. Moore where I tried to explain Articles 8 and 9, referring to what he knew or what was the situation during the Vukovar trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall a discussion about why that issue might be relevant in this case, whether with Mr. Moore or anyone else?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't have the -- the -- the taskings here with the ten points and 17 points in front of me but I believe that they include a discussion of the subordination of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. But did you have a conversation -- and now I'm not limiting myself only to prior to December of 2007. I mean from the time you -- from December 2006 to the present, have you ever had a conversation with anyone in the Office of the Prosecutor about the relevance of that issue of the subordination of the military police in this case.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to make a distinction, for obvious reasons, between the time-period before the filing of the report and the time-period after the filing of the report, and the time-period before the filing of the report I see three important stages. First, table of contents, December 2006; second, first draft, March 2007; third, submission of the final draft and feedback to the final draft in December 2008. We have addressed the time-period before the filing of the report in my previous answers. After the filing of the report, indeed, I was contacted at different occasions by members of the team to explain what, for example, what I had written in the report or to clarify to them what Articles 8 and 9 of the 1994 rules on military police mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And who specifically did you have conversations with about Articles 8 and 9 of the rules of the military police?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember well, at least with Ms. Mahindaratne, probably also Mr. Shakhmetov and Mr. Morris in relation to -- I'm not sure when -- I'm trying to think -- the document which is known as D35, it is not included in my report because I couldn't -- I didn't manage to find it. And I'm not sure whether my views were asked about that document without me knowing that it was D35 prior -- I mean, after the filing of the report but prior to it being tendered as D35, or whether I was only asked to express my views on D35 after it had been filed as D35.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, after you filed the report, were you in fact assisting, for example, Ms. Mahindaratne, in understanding issues related to the subordination of the military police?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I answered to questions she had. So that could be described as assistance, providing assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: When -- first of all, how many occasions did you have conversations with Ms. Mahindaratne about the military police, after the filing of your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall exactly. Two, three, times. I remember that once she announced that a military police witness would -- or a witness belonging to the military police would testify and she asked me a number of questions by e-mail about -- about documents or -- she -- she was planning to use. And again to explain what D35 meant. Yeah, and I answered to that -- to those e-mails or that e-mail as I would do to any other e-mail I receive from members of the OTP. I mean, that's my task as a military intelligence analyst or an intelligence analyst, "military," within the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In addition to Ms. Mahindaratne, how many other members of the trial team did you provide assistance to, in terms of understanding issues? For example, do you recall if you had any conversations with Mr. Gustafson about discipline, or e-mail communications?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you wish to -- should I only address Ms. Gustafson or also address other members of the team?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: All members of the team including Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. As I mentioned, I sometimes -- when it was possible to me I tried to follow trial proceedings, and I remember that there was discussion of the Krajina Express, this armoured train the Krajina Serbs had, in court or during the proceedings so I had no other urgent task for the other cases I work on at that time and I looked for pictures of the Krajina Express on the Internet, and I sent it to -- I don't know whether who exactly the lawyer was who was leading the witness but I most likely sent an e-mail to the case manager with those pictures. I also remember, for example, a discussion on the Krajina Liberation Army in court and I knew the -- the concept of Krajina Liberation Army from my work in the UNTAES mission, and I thought that in the context of the role, at least as I see my role in this organisation, is try to contribute in establishing facts where I believe that I have knowledge which could assist in establishing facts, I believe that it was useful for me then to send this information I had to the members of the Office of the Prosecutor or, more particularly, the case manager who was in court at that time. In relation to Ms. Gustafson, I sent her an e-mail -- I think it was during the cross-examination of -- of Ms. Botteri, but because, again, I had time to check the various court proceedings, I also try to keep an eye on what was happening in the Perisic case because I have to -- or I have been requested to compile a report for that case. I checked the other cases, also the Seselj trial where I'm a military analyst, and I saw that Ms. Botteri was testifying. I found it very important or interesting because I have seen a lot of documents signed by her, or addressed to her. And I think I'm not -- I don't recall exactly what the e-mail was about but I think it had to do with -- that documents she was using were also included in my report. But again, I'm not entirely sure that that was the matter. I mean, the documents she had used or that the Defence had used in cross-examination, that these documents were also included in my report. But I had no contact whatsoever with Ms. Gustafson prior to the testimony of Ms. Botteri.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall any other member of the trial team that you provided assistance to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, and these are all snippets but that's -- I apologise, these are -- I mean, how it went. I remember seeing a video, an evacuation video of the -- where the SVK was organizing an evacuation exercise in a particular area and then I checked on the map where this area -- where this municipality or town was located, and I sent an e-mail to -- certainly to the case manager but also -- maybe also to Mr. Hedaraly about the location -- I mean the grid reference and then the distance to the confrontation line of that particular municipality. And again, I thought that this assistance is in line with the tasks you have as an intelligence analyst, "military," within the Office of the Prosecutor. And, I mean, just to emphasise this was all after the filing of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, do you recall watching the testimony of any witnesses who used to be members of the Croatian military police? Just do you recall.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I don't remember the name of the person, and I didn't follow it in its entirety because I had other tasks to do, for other cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do the names of witness Dzolic or witness Simic ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- not specifically. It may be possible but have no -- I cannot link the name to a particular position or rank or unit in the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Finally on this issue of the military police, do you recall telling Ms. Mahindaratne that it was your assessment that the military police was operationally subordinated to General Gotovina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that follows from the discussions we had on Articles 8 and 9 from P880 which were held --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question, Mr. Theunens, was whether you recall telling her and that, of course, does not follow from the substance of what your message may have been. You told her. That would be an answer to the question. And I take it that if you tell her something that you would tell her what you think is the right thing to tell her. But the question was simply whether you told her this, that it was your assessment that the military police was operationally subordinated to General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall telling her that you -- it was your conclusion that the military police was not operationally subordinated to General Lausic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not specifically. I mean, I remember that I explained -- okay, how it -- subordination in according with the regulations works, and therefore, as I put in my report, my conclusion was that -- or is that the military police -- I mean, is subordinated to the operational commander, according to the operational chain. I did explain to her as well as, most likely, also Mr. Moore what I understood under the professional chain, i.e., to explain the relation between the military police and units and General Lausic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: On this issue of your conversation with Mr. Moore about the subordination of the military police, looking at the time-frame, that conversation took place before the Prosecutor filed his -- the pre-trial brief in this case. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when the pre-trial brief was filed. I remember talking about such issues with Mr. Moore in the December to March 2007 -- excuse me, December 2006 to March 2007 time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you -- shifting gears for one moment. You mentioned this document that you're -- supplemental information sheet and you said that paragraph 23 was altered, and you didn't pay attention when you signed it that a sentence had been deleted. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should be more precise. I have a copy here of information sheet which dates the 11th of November. And I also found a copy of the sheet you showed last evening and basically from the supplemental information sheet as I saw it, paragraph 20 is missing, part of 21 is missing, 22 is missing, 23 is missing, and part of 26 are missing. And I -- I'm very surprised by that. I don't know what happened. And I would be very grateful if somebody could explain me because, for me, paragraph 23 of the information sheet as I have it, explains everything and would also explain what happened on the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, who deleted those paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I mean, if I were authorised to speak to the Office of the Prosecutor, I would obviously have asked them but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Who did you receive -- let me ask you a different question. Did you draft the original?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. And on the 11th of November -- I had a cover sheet of an e-mail, but on the 11th of November at 11.30 a.m., I received the final version from Mr. Du-Toit. The distinction between what I had put and the final version is that Mr. Du-Toit had included annex numbers, which I didn't know. I mean I knew that a number of things would be attached to the supplementary information sheet but I didn't know whether it would be Annex A, B, or C. There was also an ERN that was missing. As I mentioned, I drafted a draft article for a conference in Oslo in September, and the article is not finished but it was considered useful to attach the article or the draft to the supplemental information sheet and that implied that the draft article first had to be ERNed by a member of the team, and that was the kind of information I -- that was added in the final version I received and I have a recollection that I signed it, and then I assumed that that would be disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions other than I would appreciate if we could perhaps get a copy of the original version that Mr. Theunens has. And I also have a matter to address with the Chamber outside the presence of the witness, whether now or when we come back from the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Theunens, would you willing to share the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- two versions of that document. Madam Usher, could you please receive them. They will be copied then, Mr. Theunens, and you will -- your copies will be returned to you. How much time would you need, Mr. Misetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No more than two minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No more than two minutes. Then I will do it before the break because that might cause us to think about matters and then we have the whole break to do that. Mr. Theunens, could you please follow Madam Usher and leave the courtroom. We'd like to see you back after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The issue I wish to address is again in light of the witness's answers concerning assistance that he provided to the trial team. I'm aware of precedent in the Vukovar case where the Trial Chamber excluded Mr. Coo, who the witness has referenced several times here, who is the head of the unit to which Mr. Theunens belongs. The testimony of Witness Coo was excluded because of his involvement with the trial team. To me, it is now at least an issue that needs to be explored because has he now testified to certain matters, I think we can see that there may be some inconsistent recollections or additional information that perhaps the Office of the Prosecutor could provide as to Mr. Theunens' role from the submission of the report to the present and how much involvement he may have had in providing any kind of opinions to members of the trial team on issues that are in dispute in this trial because the Defence may wish to raise those issues in light of the precedent from the Vukovar trial. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. First of all, I think the Phil Coo issue was in the Slobodan Milosevic case not in the Vukovar case. But the issue at that time was that Mr. Coo was involved in the preparation of the Slobodan Milosevic. I think he interviewed the witnesses. That all didn't happen in relation to Mr. Theunens. He was completely separate, he didn't interview any witnesses, he didn't make any suggestions as, you know, what question should be put to these people. It is a different issue once a report has been filed. Obviously Mr. Theunens is part of OTP. He is employed, he is paid by the UN to provide opinions and there is absolutely nothing wrong with him doing that after the report has been filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're still at the stage of gathering factual information, whether there is anything wrong or not I think Mr. Misetic had not yet reached that point. He said that he referred to a precedent in which, apparently, there may have been something wrong and that this has had consequences in that case, so that we can at least start looking at it. And thank you very much for informing us that it was the Milosevic case rather than -- if would you have more details as the date of the decision and whether it is a public decision so we can already start reading it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I will check with Mr. Waespi. My understanding -- I recall that it was Judge Parker who gave the decision but I could be wrong on that as well. You're absolutely right, Mr. President. I just want to be able to gather the facts, and it may very well be that Mr. Waespi's correct, but I think we should have a opportunity to inspect it for ourselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I might put some questions to the witness I had already on my mind which might be relevant for this issue just after the break. We'll have a break until quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I would have a few follow-up questions, in relation to your testimony during the first afternoon session. You told us that you watched some of the proceedings. You said, I had time. Were you specifically tasked to follow the proceedings, either by saying, Follow them as much as you can, or was it just personal interest, or did ever any of your colleagues or superiors ask you to watch, to the extent possible, or to watch specific portions, was there ever any request?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, in my recollection, it was on my personal initiative when I would -- in the morning I would check my agenda, check the court schedule, and then flip from one courtroom to the other because, for example, I work on other trials, and if there was a witness, sometimes somebody I knew from former UN or ECMM, or, for example, I tried to follow Kosta Novakovic because I knew -- not personally, of course, but I knew his name and his position from the time I was serving UNPROFOR. So that was the level of -- that was how I came about to follow proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you had communication in which you explained to members of the Prosecution team certain matters, sometimes, I do understand, in a meeting you were asked questions. Did you also sometimes take the initiative and why did you do that, if you did, something struck you when looking at the screen, what -- what moved you to -- to get in touch then with members of the team, if you did so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, you are asking me about a meeting and then the screen, does the screen refer to trial proceedings or to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No, the screen you're watching, you're following the proceedings. Something came into your mind as it might interest one of the team members, and did you then, on your own initiative, send them an e-mail, call them? Did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would send them e-mails, Your Honour, on my own initiative. I cannot exclude that I have received an e-mail from somebody to explain something that they considered relevant. When I say somebody, a member of the -- of the legal team. But the problem I have, I work simultaneously on several cases and in, like, for example, in the four other cases where I was directly involved in the investigation and even interviewed witnesses, I was much closer involved. Even in the -- in -- now with the Seselj trial, which is still ongoing, I receive continuous questions, and at this moment I cannot make a clear distinction whether I received only e-mails for Seselj or also for Gotovina. My recollection at this moment is that if I received e-mails in relation to the trial proceedings for the Gotovina trial, that the number is extremely limited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is, less than five, less then ten, less than 30, what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Less than five, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Less than five.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And when you would compare the number of e-mails, Gotovina trial e-mail, in/out, receiving less than five, sending over total maybe 20, 30, it's difficult to say for me. And they dealt with issues where I believed, just to answer the last part of your question, that the knowledge and the experience I have of the conflict could assist in establishing the facts. I come from a civil law system, Your Honours, not from a common law system and I realize that have I problems with the common law system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know yet how to interpret this last observation, Mr. Theunens, but I'll give it some time to ... You mean by finding your position in the common law system if you work in the Office of the Prosecution. Is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honours. The Article -- actually the conference I gave in Oslo, the speech I gave, my suggestion was -- and also based on the experience of Phil Coo in a previous trial was that, actually, experts should be called or would best be called by the Trial Chamber whereby, and again, I'm not a lawyer but I was just looking at it from the analytical point of view, the parties would submit all evidence that they want the expert to review to the Trial Chamber and then the expert would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that you are in favour of a different system which is not unfamiliar to me but let's -- I now understand your earlier observation. These were my questions. Mr. Kay, are you ready to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There was just follow-up while we're on this to try and deal with all matters which is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: His Honour mentioned meetings. One matter that I'd like to know is have you had meetings with the investigators for the OTP? Now the names that come to my mind are Mr. Foster, Mr. Casey, and Mr. Morris, whom you've mentioned several times, who are men who have interviewed witnesses for the OTP. I would ask you to declare what -- what those contacts have been, the type of contacts, and the type of discussions.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never had a -- what I would call a formal meeting with Mr. Foster or Mr. Casey. I remember seeing Mr. Casey once in Zagreb when I was there on another interview mission, but we just crossed each other in the hotel, and as I said, courtesy. Mr. Foster once came -- or maybe twice came to sit at a table where I was having coffee here in the office with Mr. Morris. In relation to Mr. Morris who is actually a member of the Military Analysis Team, i.e., intelligence analyst, military, we had meetings, team meetings, I mean Military Analysis Team meetings, exchanges of views about analysis, or social gatherings. He has been my colleague for at least seven and a half years. He, for example -- received me when I arrived at the ICTY in June 2001 but I had never a Gotovina-related meeting with Mr. Moric [sic] with the exception of the conversations we had about the spreadsheets that were addressed earlier. Mr. Van Rooyen is another investigator assigned to the Gotovina team, and he and I, we have a social relationship based on our close cooperation in -- in the investigation for the Vukovar case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The team meetings you referred to, what are those team meetings?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were meetings of the Military Analysis Team. They were held at irregular intervals, sometimes every month -- I'm now talking about the situation in 2001, 2004. Later there were less meetings and these were mainly meetings where the team leader, the latest -- the last team leader was Mr. Coo, would gather the analysts to discuss general issues, communication of information he had obtained as to the internal organisation of the OTP, specific military analytical issues, and so on, but nothing specific to the Gotovina case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So just to deal with this issue so it's clear, in relation to Mr. Morris, has there been any discussions between you and he about the evidence of a witness named Lausic? And that's the Lausic who is the General Lausic, chief of administration, chief of the military police administration. Have you and he had discussions, informally or formally, in any way about the nature of his statement or information from him?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I -- I think I asked Mr. Morris once informally, and that may well have been prior to the filing of the report, whether Mr. Lausic was interviewed and whether -- or whether he would testify. And he answered the question that he was interviewed but that he didn't know that he -- whether he would testify or not, and that's the level at which we discussed Mr. Lausic, or General Lausic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That's all I ask on the matters, because Your Honour, mentioned meetings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let us return to the matters we were dealing with yesterday. I had one more document, Mr. Theunens, to deal with in that sequence before we close, as His Honour to deal with matters just before the end, but it would be important for me to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's a document dated the 6th of October, 1995. It's from the Split Military District Command. It deals with an inspection of Split Military District units and when that inspection will take place in October 1995, concerning the level of organisation, capability.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we go to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Training, all general issues concerning the state of the Military District units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we go to page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The order there, as to what is to happen in relation to this inspection, if we just go to the last page. And you'll recollect the documents we looked -- we looked at about five important documents relating to the Split Military District at the end of my questions yesterday. And down here, we see the various people within the Split Military District, including the garrisons included in this, and you will notice no Knin ZM. Again, would you agree with me that this is a highly significant omission, in relation to the issue concerning the Split Military District and the relationship of the Knin garrison with the Military District units?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that on the first page it is indicated that this concerns an inspection by members of the HV Main Staff --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- who will inspect units and commands of the Split Military District, and indeed the Knin garrison is -- is not mentioned among the addressee list. I haven't seen everything in the document, but it would be logical that the addressee list includes the units that will be subjected to the inspection. Now why the HV Main Staff decides not to inspect the Knin garrison is something I have no information on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That, then, deals with that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1006, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1006 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We'll go to a new topic now and it was one that you mentioned earlier in your testimony and I said we'd be coming to it because you said you didn't know the nature of Mr. Cermak's background, and so we will just be looking quickly at some documents concerning his appointment and background.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And if we, first of all, go to 65 ter 5803 -- 5830, my apologies, Madam Registrar [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
